output.title: Privacy is not workflow control
output.body:
If you are considering AI in a small business, privacy promises are only part of the decision. A vendor can tell you where data is stored, how it is protected, or what terms apply. That still does not answer the more practical question: who can act on the data once it enters your workflow.

That is the bounded decision I would make first. For any repeatable process such as invoice handling or customer replies, decide whether the AI is allowed to take action on its own, or whether it only recommends an action and waits for human approval. For money movement and other high-risk decisions, human approval stays mandatory. That is Bareni policy, not a warranty.

Why this matters: privacy terms do not control your own approval steps. If the workflow is loose, the best privacy statement in the world will not fix it. If the workflow is tight, you can use AI without handing over the keys to the shop.

A simple diagnostic question helps: will I see the input, the reasoning, and the recommended action before anything is committed?

Next step: map your most repeated workflow, mark the points where money, customer communication, or data deletion could happen, and decide which of those points must stay human-approved.
